{"evidence":[{"sentence_id":0,"text":"\"The Loneliness of the Long-Distance Runner\" is a short story by Alan Sillitoe, published in 1959 as part of a short story collection of the same name.","title":"The Loneliness of the Long-Distance Runner"},{"sentence_id":1,"text":" The work focuses on Smith, a poor Nottingham teenager from a dismal home in a working class area, who has bleak prospects in life and few interests beyond petty crime.","title":"The Loneliness of the Long-Distance Runner"},{"sentence_id":2,"text":" The boy turns to long-distance running as a method of both an emotional and a physical escape from his situation.","title":"The Loneliness of the Long-Distance Runner"},{"sentence_id":3,"text":" The story was adapted for a 1962 film of the same title, with Sillitoe writing the screenplay and Tony Richardson directing.","title":"The Loneliness of the Long-Distance Runner"},{"sentence_id":4,"text":" The part of Smith (now called Colin) was played by Tom Courtenay.","title":"The Loneliness of the Long-Distance Runner"},{"sentence_id":0,"text":"NGC 3324 is an open cluster in the southern constellation Carina, located northwest of the Carina Nebula (NGC 3372) at a distance of 2317 pc from Earth.","title":"NGC 3324"},{"sentence_id":1,"text":" It is closely associated with the emission nebula IC 2599 , also known as Gum 31 .","title":"NGC 3324"},{"sentence_id":2,"text":" The two are often confused as a single object, and together have been nicknamed the \"Gabriela Mistral Nebula\" due to its resemblance to the Chilean poet.","title":"NGC 3324"},{"sentence_id":3,"text":" NGC 3324 was first catalogued by James Dunlop in 1826.","title":"NGC 3324"}],"peer_messages":[],"previous_answer":"writer","question":"Gabriela Mistral and Alan Sillitoe were both in what profession?"}
